# STEP 1 — Master Directory Structure & Architecture

```
local/
├── package.json                  # three@0.160.1 (pinned), vite@5.4.19 (dev) — nothing else
├── vite.config.js                # Multi-page build: one entry per game folder (one line added per game)
├── .gitignore
│
├── shared/                       # ── GAME-AGNOSTIC LAYER (zero imports from any game folder) ──
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── Engine.js             # Renderer / scene / camera / RAF loop, global timescale (hit-stop
│   │   │                         #   hook), DPR-aware resize, and a full-graph dispose() that walks
│   │   │                         #   the scene and frees every geometry, material, and texture
│   │   ├── Input.js              # Unified dual-input: WASD/Arrows + Gamepad API mapped to the same
│   │   │                         #   action names; polled axes + edge-triggered pressed()/released()
│   │   ├── ObjectPool.js         # Generic pre-allocated pool (acquire/release, zero runtime alloc)
│   │   ├── ParticleManager.js    # THE single particle system: one InstancedMesh, hard cap 500 live
│   │   │                         #   instances, per-instance velocity/gravity/life, instanceColor
│   │   ├── CameraShake.js        # Trauma-based (0→1), exponential decay, impact-velocity scaling,
│   │   │                         #   Simplex-driven offset + roll
│   │   ├── HitStop.js            # Brief timescale dilation (e.g. 1.0 → 0.05 for 60–120 ms)
│   │   ├── Shockwave.js          # Pooled expanding emissive rings (RingGeometry, additive fade)
│   │   ├── MotionTrail.js        # Fading ribbon trail (dynamic BufferGeometry) for fast movers
│   │   ├── FloatingText.js       # 3D→screen-projected HTML score popups, glassmorphism styled
│   │   ├── Audio.js              # WebAudio: synthesized SFX (osc + noise) + generative music loop
│   │   │                         #   (lookahead scheduler), master bus, mute
│   │   └── ProceduralTextures.js # Canvas texture factory: neon grid floor, radial glow sprite,
│   │                             #   panel/scanline textures — all cached, all disposable
│   ├── post/
│   │   └── PostFX.js             # EffectComposer + RenderPass + UnrealBloomPass, tuned so emissive
│   │                             #   surfaces glow without washing to white (threshold/strength/radius)
│   └── utils/
│       ├── Math.js               # clamp / lerp / damp / rand / angle helpers
│       └── Noise.js              # Simplex noise (geometry displacement, camera shake, trails)
│
└── [GameName]/                   # ── ONE FOLDER PER NAMED GAME, EXACTLY NAMED ──
    ├── index.html                # Game entry point (Vite multi-page input)
    ├── main.js                   # Bootstrap: Engine + PostFX + Audio + UI, wires the loop, teardown
    ├── Game.js                   # State machine (menu/playing/paused/gameover), score, lives, win/loss
    ├── <Entity>.js               # Game-specific entities (e.g. Ball.js, Paddle.js) — hand-written physics
    ├── Arena.js                  # Procedural environment: court, walls, emitters, lighting rig
    └── UI.js                     # Glassmorphism HUD: score, lives, menus, pause, win/loss screens
```

**Vite strategy.** One project at the root, multi-page: `vite.config.js` lists each game's `index.html` as a build input, so every game is an isolated entry with its own bundle. Games import the shared layer via relative paths (`../../shared/core/Engine.js`); Three.js addons resolve through the package's exports map (`three/addons/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js`). Dependency direction is strictly one-way: `game → shared → three`. No game ever imports another game; nothing in `shared/` knows a game exists.

**Shared-utilities strategy.** The six required VFX (shake, particles, hit-stop, trails, shockwaves, floating text) live *only* in `shared/core/` and are composed by every game — so the next game in the collection gets all of them for free. `ParticleManager` is the single allocation point for particles (one `InstancedMesh`, 500-instance hard cap enforced by the manager, not by callers). `ObjectPool` is generic so each game pools its own entities (balls, bricks, enemies) with zero per-frame allocation. `Engine.dispose()` guarantees teardown: it walks the scene graph and calls `.dispose()` on every geometry, material, and texture, and the texture factory keeps a registry so canvas textures are freed exactly once.

---

## Compliance Statement

**Anti-Lazy Directive.** Every function I write is fully implemented and production-ready. No `// ... rest of function`, no `// insert logic here`, no `// previously defined code`, no stubbed methods. If an output is truncated mid-file, I stop at the exact character and resume verbatim on "continue" — no preamble, no restart.

**Strict Memory Management.** All projectiles, entities, and particles are pre-allocated and pooled; the hot update path performs zero allocations. Particles are capped at 500 by the centralized manager. `InstancedMesh` is used for particles and any repeated geometry (rings, trail segments, repeated arena props). Every geometry, material, and texture created is tracked and explicitly `.dispose()`d on teardown — no orphans, no leaks.

**Sequential Output Protocol.** I will not generate the collection. I will not implement any game you have not named. Each step waits on your explicit trigger: "Begin [Game Name]" for the plan, "Plan approved" for implementation, "continue" for truncation recovery.
